To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pyrazoles and triazoles are alkylated with cis- andtrans-1,4-DCB to give polymeric salts and that the monoalkylated products of pyrazole with cis-DCBand 1,2-dialkylated products of triazole with cis- and tran-DCB undergo dehydrochlorination to give 1-(buta-dien-2-yl)-pyrazoles and -1,2, 4-triazoles.
The phase-transfer catalysed alkylation of azoles with dichloroalkenes leads to a variety of interesting products.

the alkylation of azoles with cis- and/or trans-1, 4-dichlorobutene-2 is a phase-transfer catalyed reaction, and that the monoalkylation products undergo further reaction to form bicyclic salts or polymeric quaternaries, depending on the structure of the azole.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the preparation of 1-(buta-1,3-dien-2-yl)-pyrazoles and 5-(butadienyl)-1,2, 4-triazoles, and with the study of their reactions.
the phase-transfer catalyze (PTC) reactions of pyrazoles, 1,2-4-triazoles, and related heterocycles.
the synthesis and reactions of 1-(2-butenyl)- and 1-(4-butenyl) pyrazoles and pyrimidines, and 1-(buten-2-ynyl)pyrazole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PTC alkylation of azoles with 1,4-dihalides is not a useful synthetic procedure.
the PTC alkylation of azoles with cis- or trans-DCB leads to different results depending on the structure of the azole.

PTC reactions of pyrazoles, 1,2-dihydro-1,2,3-triazoles, and 1,3,5-triazines with cis-1,4-DCB are not feasible because the intermediate monoalkylated products undergo cyclization to bicyclic salts which cannot be converted to the monoalkylated compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alkylation of azoles with cis-1,4-disubstituted-2-buten-1-ones is a facile process, whereas the alkylation with the corresponding 2-butenes requires a phase transfer catalytic system and is accompanied by side reactions.

phase-transfer catalyze alkylation of azoles with cis- and/or trans-1,2-dichloroethenes leads to a variety of products depending on the structure and nature of the azole and the nature of the 1,2-dihaloethene used.
PTC alkylation of azoles with cis- and/or trans-1,2-dichloroethylenes leads to the formation of polyquaternary salts, while the corresponding 1,4-dialkenyl compounds are not formed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase-transfer catalyed (PTC) reaction of cis- and trans-DCHB with 1, 2, 4-triazole is a convenient method for preparation of 1-alkyl-1H-1,2, 4triazole-3-thiones.
the PTC reaction of azoles with DCB is a convenient and efficient route to 1-(4-bromo-2-butynyl)-, 1-(4-azido-2-butyn-1-yl)-, and 1-(4-amino-2-butyn)-1,2,3-triazoles.
cis-DCB reacts with pyrazoles in a phase-transfer catalyze fashion to give the corresponding bicyclic quaternary ammonium salts, whereas trans-DCB does not.
